rationale: While early reports of NFU1-associated hereditary spastic paraplegia (SPG93) described slowly evolving, non-fatal white matter abnormalities without prominent necrosis in contrast to infantile-lethal MMDS1, subsequent investigations demonstrate that the neuroimaging presentation exists along a phenotypic spectrum. Notably, patients presenting with childhood-onset spastic paraparesis can exhibit partial cystic degeneration and cavitation in cerebral white matter, directly contradicting the claim that SPG93 is consistently characterized by mild, non-cavitating lesions.

evidence.text: A patient with NFU1 mutation presented with a milder spastic paraplegia phenotype characterized by later onset, slowly progressive spastic paraparesis with relapsing-remitting episodes, mild cognitive impairment, long survival, and slowly evolving leukoencephalopathy without rapid cavitation.

source.title: New spastic paraplegia phenotype associated to mutation of NFU1
source.quote: We report a new NFU1 mutated patient presenting with a milder phenotype characterized by a later onset, a slowly progressive spastic paraparesis with relapsing-remitting episodes, mild cognitive impairment and a long survival. The early white matter abnormalities observed on MRI was combined with a mixed sensory-motor neuropathy in the third decade. Our case clearly suggests the importance of considering NFU1 mutation in slowly evolving leukoencephalopathy with high glycine concentration.

evidence.text: A 27-month-old female with homozygous NFU1 mutation presented clinically with spastic paraparesis and a relapsing-remitting course; neuroimaging demonstrated frontal white matter hyperintensity accompanied by partial cystic degeneration and cavitation.

source.title: A genetic mimic of cerebral palsy: Homozygous NFU1 mutation with marked intrafamilial phenotypic variation
source.quote: This report documents the case of a 27-month-old girl, who showed clinical signs and symptoms of spastic paraparesis with a relapsing-remitting course... Magnetic resonance imaging revealed hyperintensity of the cerebral white matter that was more prominent in the frontal regions, with milder involvement in the posterior periventricular regions. There was also evidence of partial cystic degeneration and cavitation in the frontal regions.

evidence.text: A cohort analysis delineated a phenotypic continuum of NFU1-related disorders spanning from early-onset rapidly fatal leukoencephalopathy to pure or complex hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP).

conflicts: Uzunhan et al. (2020) demonstrated that an individual with NFU1 mutation presenting with spastic paraparesis had cystic degeneration and frontal cavitation on MRI, contradicting the hypothesis that SPG93 neuroimaging is exclusively non-cavitating.
Multiple cohorts note that NFU1 phenotypes exist as a continuum rather than a dichotomous non-cavitating versus cavitating leukoencephalopathy division.

new_directions.question_text: What specific NFU1 variant locations or residual iron-sulfur cluster assembly activities correlate with the development of cavitating versus non-cavitating white matter lesions?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying genotype-phenotype correlations could explain why some patients with spastic paraplegia develop cystic cavitations while others exhibit only stable/slowly evolving periventricular hyperintensities.

new_directions.question_text: Does serial brain MRI during relapsing-remitting episodes in SPG93 reveal transient cavitation or cystic necrosis that subsequently resolves or stabilizes?
new_directions.rationale: Documenting longitudinal neuroimaging changes during acute metabolic or clinical decompensations would resolve whether cavitation is stage-dependent in milder SPG93 presentations.
